**Description:** With this function block an internal clock (Real Time Clock RTC) can be implemented in the TwinCAT PLC. When the function block is enabled via bEn, the RTC clock is initialized with the current NT system time. One system cycle of the CPU is used to calculate the current RTC time. The function block must be called once per PLC cycle in order for the current time to be calculated. Within the function block, an instance of the function blocks NT_GetTime, FB_GetTimeZoneInformation and RTC_EX2 is called. The time is output at the outputs stSysTi for the read system time and stUtc for the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). This is determined internally from the system time and the time zone. If the system time and/or the time zone was entered incorrectly, the UTC time will also be wrong.

**Description:** When activated, the function block FB_BA_WrtPersistDat first saves the persistent data in the Port_xxx.bootdata file. It is not necessary to explicitly specify the port or runtime system at which the PLC is located; this is determined internally. Once the data has been written, the content of the file Port_xxx.bootdata is copied to the backup file Port_xxx.bootdata-old. Thus both files are always synchronized. In case the original file with the persistent data is not readable, the backup copy, which is then read, contains the same data.

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

**Description:** This function block prevents pumps or actuators from blocking after long periods without movement by outputting a switch-on pulse. The maximum duration of the standstill until a pulse is output is determined by the value of udiTiOffMin_sec. For logging the idle time, the input bFdb must be linked to the operating feedback from the aggregate. The length of the pulse is parameterized with udiTiImplLngt_sec. The input bExe should be used if the anti- blocking protection pulses are to be issued cyclically based on a schedule, rather than depending on the idle times. A rising edge at bExe immediately triggers output of a pulse to bQ. Generally, a pulse output only occurs if the function block at bEn is enabled.

| `udiNumOfElem` | `Size of the FIFO buffer. A change resets the previous averaging. Internally limited to a` | — |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rOut` | `REAL` | — |
| `rMax` | `REAL` | — |
| `rMin` | `REAL` | — |

| `rMin` | `Smallest value in the FIFO buffer.` | — |

**Description:** The function block FB_BA_TiAvrg calculates the arithmetic mean value of an analog value that was logged over a certain period. Discrete values are written into a FIFO buffer. udiIntval_sec specifies the time interval [s] over which the values are logged and written into the FIFO. Values are written if the input bEn is TRUE. The variable udiNumOfElem is used to determine the size of the FIFO buffer. It is limited to 1..512. The function block can be used for calculating an hourly mean outside temperature over a day, for example. In this case udiNumOfElem would be 24 and udiIntval_sec would be 3600 seconds. bEn is the general enable of the function block. If bEn = FALSE, the FIFO buffer within the function block is deleted completely, and no data are recorded.

These are in detail: • Resulting telegram building alarms • Protection telegram Fire The FB_BA_FireAlarmSystem [} 859] template supplies the information "Fire alarm" via a globally declared structure variable stBuildingAlarms (see global variable list Site [} 718]). If this alarm is active, the blinds are raised completely via a FB_BA_SunBldEvt [} 377]. • Protection telegram Burglar The FB_BA_BurglarAlarmSystem [} 858] template supplies the information "burglar alarm" via a globally declared structure variable stBuildingAlarms (see global variable list Site [} 718]). If this alarm is active, the blinds are raised completely via a FB_BA_SunBldEvt [} 377]. ## 8. Implementation roadmap

Phases are ordered by dependency, not by category size. Each phase ends
with the affected libraries compiling and passing simulator vectors.

Landed (detail pruned; git history retains it, as-built status lives in
`docs/plc/compat/README.md`):

- **C0 — Compat package format**: `tplcc build --library` +
  `--lib` source inclusion + per-library docs under
  `docs/plc/compat/twincat/`.
- **C1 — T0 core**: Tc2_Math (8/8) and Tc2_Standard (31/31) complete;
  Tc2_Utilities BCD pair + `FB_EnumStringNumbers`. Remainder of
  Tc2_Utilities needs `PVOID`/union types — blocked on language
  features, not effort.
- **C2 — T1 services I**: `tplc-net`/`tplc-serial`/`tplc-ads`
  services + `FB_Socket`/`FB_Serial`/`FB_Ads` + Tc2 wrappers, all
  with real end-to-end tests. Leftovers: DNS resolution and
  multicast in `tplc-net`; full AMS router/server and configurable
  local NetID in `tplc-ads`.

| Phase | Deliverable | Unblocks |
|---|---|---|
| **C3 — T1 services II** | done: RealtimeMonitoring (`tplc-rtmon` + `FB_RtMon` + Tc3 wrappers, `tc3_rtmon` ctest); blocked: DynamicMemory (PVOID), Module (COM object model), JsonXml (METHOD/interface/POINTER/REFERENCE/HRESULT), EventLogger (I_Tc* interfaces, HRESULT, GUID) | Standard remainder |
| **C4 — Connectivity wave 1** | in progress: Tc2_ModbusSrv done 20/20 (`tplc-modbus` TCP+UDP + `FB_Modbus` + all TCP/UDP wrappers, `tc2_modbussrv` ctest) + Tc2_ModbusRTU V2-master subset (`tplc-modbus` ABI v3 RTU transport + `FB_ModbusRtu` + ten master-action wrappers, `tc2_modbusrtu` ctest; slave/Generic/KL6x variants remain) + Tc3_sACN data path (`tplc-sacn` E1.31 codec + multicast source/receiver + `FB_SacnSource`/`FB_SacnReceiver` + poll-model wrappers + three IEC helpers, `tc3_sacn` ctest; `I_sAcn*` interface model remains) + Tc3_BACnetRev14 protocol layer (`tplc-bacnet` BACnet/IP BVLC/NPDU/APDU codec + Who-Is/I-Am + ReadProperty/WriteProperty + `FB_Bacnet` + three poll-model wrappers, `tc3_bacnet` ctest; catalog's 3 entries are device-config/doc examples — TwinCAT's generated-device model, COV/events/segmentation/router remain) + Tc3_PJLink protocol layer (`tplc-pjlink` PJLink TCP client on 4352 + MD5 nonce/password auth + `PJLINK ERRA`/`ERR1` handling + `FB_Pjlink` + `FB_PJLink`/`_Power`/`_Input`/`_Mute` poll-model wrappers, `tc3_pjlink` ctest; TwinCAT's auto-managed object — keep-alive, status polling, AMS NetID, I_TcMessage, EventLogger, HRESULT methods — remains a documented gap) + Tc3_S7Comm + Tc2_S5S7Com protocol layer (`tplc-s7` S7comm RFC1006 client on TCP 102 — TPKT/COTP/S7comm codec verified byte-exact vs python-snap7 — persistent session + Read/Write Var + Setup Comm + S7-Any byte/bit addressing + `FB_S7Conn`/`FB_S7Io` + `FB_S7_Connect`/`_Read`/`_Write`/`_ReadBit`/`_WriteBit` poll-model wrappers, `tc3_s7comm` ctest; request-queue/cyclic-request/PVOID/HRESULT/AMS model and S5 3964/PKW remain documented gaps) + Tc2_FTP+Tc3_FTP protocol layer (`tplc-ftp` RFC 959 client on TCP 21 with PASV passive data connections — line-based control channel, USER/PASS login, TYPE I/PASV/RETR/STOR/LIST sequencing — `FB_FtpConn`/`FB_FtpCmd`/`FB_FtpXfer` builtins + `FB_FTP_Connect`/`_Cmd`/`_Download`/`_Upload`/`_List`/`_MkDir`/`_RemoveDir`/`_DeleteFile`/`_FileExists`/`_DirExists`/`_Rename` poll-model wrappers covering the FB_FtpConnection/Explorer/Transfer objects and FB_FTP_* set, `tc3_ftp` ctest mask 0xfff; profiles/AddProfile, I_TcMessage/EventLogger/HRESULT, FB_FTP_HostResolve DNS, FTPS/TLS, SFTP/SSH, active mode, REST/MLSD remain documented gaps) + Tc2_SMS+Tc2_SMTP protocol layer (`tplc-smtp` RFC 5321 client on TCP 25 — 220/EHLO/AUTH LOGIN/MAIL/RCPT/DATA dot-stuffed/250/QUIT — `FB_SmtpSend` builtin + `FB_SmtpV3`/`FB_SmtpV3_Full`/obsolete `FB_Smtp`/`FB_SmtpFull`/`FB_SmtpAttach`/`FB_GetTcPlcSMS_Version` wrappers; GSM text-mode SMS via `FB_SendSMS`, a pure-ST AT state machine over `tplc-serial` (AT/AT+CMGF=1/AT+CMGS/`>`/text+Ctrl-Z/+CMGS/OK), `tc2_sms_sms` ctest mask 0x1ff; TLS, attachments, Cc/Bcc, multi-recipient, MIME, TwinCAT SMTP-server ADS proxy, SMS PDU/UCS2/concatenation remain documented gaps); IEC 60870 remains | Field protocols |
| **C5 — Motion core** | `tplc-motion` axis backend + PLCopen MC2 subset (`MC_Power`…`MC_TorqueControl`) | All Motion libraries |
| **C6 — Motion extended** | NC interpolation, camming, hydraulics, drives (CiA-402 via Tether DS402), MC3 | Motion remainder minus robotics |
| **C7 — T2 wave 2** | OPC UA, EtherNet/IP, IEC 61850, IoT/MQTT, OCPP, AES70, Building buses (DALI/DMX/EIB/LON/MBus/EnOcean) | Long-tail protocols |
| **C8 — Measurement/Control** | Filter, CM, Weighing, SPA, ControllerToolbox, TempController, PowerMonitoring, PackML, Plastic, QRC | Industry logic |
| **C9 — T4 engines** | Vision engine bridge, ML inference service, Analytics storage, Speech | Vision/ML/Analytics |
| **C10 — Licensed/stub** | mxAutomation, uniVAL, vision-deep-learning internals: explicit unsupported status or licensed shim | Honest coverage close-out |

### Testing strategy

- Every compat function gets L1 (MIR interp) and L2 (real runtime)
  vectors in `sim_vectors` style, plus doc-example-derived tests where
  manuals include ST snippets.
- Protocol libraries get loopback transports first (simulated peer),
  then hardware-in-loop.
- Motion FBs get state-machine conformance tests against the PLCopen
  specification tables, independent of the axis backend (mock axes).
- Coverage is measured against this catalog: an API is "done" when its
  entry here links to an implementation and passing tests.

### Open questions

- Binary vs source compatibility: shipping Beckhoff `.library` binaries
  is not possible; all entries are re-implemented. Source compatibility
  (same names/signatures) is the target.
- Whether `tplc-motion` should live in this repo or in the sibling
  `Tether` motion framework with a thin PLC binding.
- License boundaries for mxAutomation/uniVAL/Vision: confirm with
  Beckhoff whether any SDK license permits reimplementation.
